correctness.rationale: Blockwise minimum \(2\) is attained exactly by two states at leaf multiplicity two, and by one state at multiplicity at least three. Independence of empty core vertices plus the rainbow condition gives four ordered leaf choices for each nonisolated empty core and two for each isolated empty core; this proves \((1+2t)^iI_{G^\circ}(4t)\). The clone-blowup identity \(I_{G^{(r)}}(4)=I_G(5^r-1)\) and polynomial interpolation provide a complete Turing reduction from known \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard bipartite independent-set counting. The original-definition exhaustive verifier passed 30 base-graph cases and three separate clone-identity tests. Finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Samadi–Soltankhah, arXiv:2208.02340v2, pp. 10–12: the broad scalar theorem yields the value \(2n\) when the second factor has two isolated vertices, for base graphs without isolated vertices.
Cabrera-Martínez, Mathematics 10 (2022), 2287: the stated corona formula assumes both factors have no isolated vertices, excluding \(\overline{K_2}\).
The two-leaf and three-leaf cases have the same known minimum value but respectively nontrivial and unique optimizer profiles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known general scalar formula has broader graph-product scope in its own domain, and its special case \(\gamma=2n\) is explicitly conceded. A minimum weight by itself cannot imply the optimizer census: on equally sized bases, a three-vertex path has 29 optima while a triangle has 13, though each has weight six. The inspected prior theorem and proof do not present a complete equality-case census or restricted exact-counting theorem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior scalar minimum is a theorem strictly weaker than the current polynomial identity, which includes exact coefficients for every independent-set cardinality. The known hardness of independent-set counting does not alone establish hardness for corona optima until the label-to-independent-set bijection and interpolation reduction are proved; both are provided. For leaf multiplicity at least three, uniqueness is an equality-condition argument not entailed by the minimum value alone.

originality.rationale: The publicly available 2022 preprint (revised 2023) establishes the scalar two-leaf corona minimum for nonisolated bases, but not a full minimum-labeling independence-polynomial census or the exact-counting reduction. The 2022 prior publisher formula assumes a second factor without isolates, inapplicable to two isolated leaves. A bounded set of indexed literature, analogous formulations, and published claims disclosed no covering statement. The remaining inaccessible-publisher-text and unindexed-priority risks are recorded, not claimed eliminated.
residual_risks: The Cabrera-Martínez full article was not accessible after direct open-access attempts; its indexed formula excludes the attachment used here, but hidden related enumeration cannot be ruled out.
No mathematical database or text search can exclude all unindexed statements, thesis appendices, or future-discovered prior claims.
This is a self-review; independent validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: The result supplies all coefficients of the optimizer-distribution polynomial of a natural arbitrary-base corona family, recovers the base independence polynomial, and exhibits a sharp optimizer-multiplicity threshold at two versus three private leaves. The counting problem is hard on bipartite coronas although finding the minimum weight is immediate. This structural and algorithmic bridge is motivated by an existing corona minimum-weight theorem, not a random parameter slice.
